classification.difficultyReason: Recall the taught equilateral-triangle and right-angle constructions, then apply successive angle bisections to obtain the requested sizes. Additional bisections repeat the same method rather than require a new connection.

content.prompt: Use a ruler and compasses to construct angles of size:

answer.short: Construct an equilateral triangle; each vertex angle is $60^\circ$.
answer.worked: Draw an interval $AB$. With radius $AB$, draw arcs centred at $A$ and $B$ meeting at $C$. Draw $AC$ and $BC$. Since $AB=AC=BC$, triangle $ABC$ is equilateral and $\angle BAC=60^\circ$. Retain the construction arcs.

spec.description: Authored completed equilateral-triangle construction with equal-radius intersecting arcs.

answer.worked: Construct $\angle BAC=60^\circ$ using equal-radius arcs centred at $A$ and $B$. Draw an arc centred at $A$ meeting $AB$ and $AC$ at $D$ and $E$. With the same compass radius at $D$ and $E$, draw arcs meeting inside the angle at $P$. Draw $AP$. Then $\angle BAP=60^\circ\div2=30^\circ$. Retain the construction arcs.

spec.description: Completed 60-degree construction and its compass-constructed bisector.

answer.short: Construct $60^\circ$, bisect to obtain $30^\circ$, then bisect again.
answer.worked: Construct a $60^\circ$ angle using the equilateral-triangle construction. Bisect it using an arc from the vertex and equal-radius intersecting arcs from the two points on its arms. Repeat this bisection construction on the resulting $30^\circ$ angle. Draw the second bisector and retain all construction arcs. The required angle is $30^\circ\div2=15^\circ$.

spec.description: Equilateral construction followed by successive bisectors at 30 and 15 degrees; construction arcs retained.

answer.short: Construct a right angle by bisecting a straight angle.
answer.worked: Draw a line through $A$. An arc centred at $A$ marks points $D$ and $E$ on opposite sides of $A$, with $AD=AE$. With equal radii greater than $AD$, draw arcs centred at $D$ and $E$ meeting at $P$. Draw $AP$. This bisects the straight angle, so $\angle EAP=180^\circ\div2=90^\circ$. Retain the construction arcs.

spec.description: Straight-angle bisection with symmetric compass arcs and a right-angle marker.

answer.worked: Construct a right angle by bisecting a straight angle. Draw an arc centred at its vertex meeting the two perpendicular arms. Draw equal-radius arcs from these two intersection points to meet inside the right angle, then join their intersection to the vertex. Retain the construction arcs. The resulting angle is $90^\circ\div2=45^\circ$.

spec.description: Constructed right angle and its compass bisector, with construction arcs.

answer.short: Construct $90^\circ$, bisect to obtain $45^\circ$, then bisect again.
answer.worked: Construct a right angle by bisecting a straight angle. Bisect the right angle using the compass angle-bisection construction to obtain $45^\circ$. Apply the same bisection construction to that $45^\circ$ angle. Draw the second bisector and retain the construction arcs. The required angle is $45^\circ\div2=22\frac12^\circ$.

spec.description: Right-angle construction followed by successive bisectors at 45 and 22½ degrees; construction arcs retained.
